items.known: CKV_AWS_46 Ensure no hard-coded secrets exist in EC2 user data (resource aws_instance.web_host)
items.issue: Plain text secrets in user data
items.remediation: Use AWS Secrets Manager or environment variables to handle sensitive data instead of hardcoding in user data

items.known: CKV_AWS_3 Ensure all data stored in the EBS is securely encrypted (resource aws_ebs_volume.web_host_storage)
items.remediation: Set the `encrypted` attribute to `true` and provide a `kms_key_id` for the encryption

items.known: CKV_AWS_24 Ensure no security groups allow ingress from 0.0.0.0:0 to port 22 (resource aws_security_group.web-node)
items.issue: Security group open to the world on SSH port
items.remediation: Restrict the `cidr_blocks` in the ingress rule for port 22 to only trusted IP ranges

scores.reason: Right direction (remove hardcoded secrets, use Secrets Manager), but vague. It doesn't name an IAM instance profile (iam_instance_profile) or say to remove the keys from user_data. 'Environment variables' alone would not fix the check if the values are still hardcoded in user_data.
Setting `encrypted = true` on aws_ebs_volume fixes CKV_AWS_3. Adding kms_key_id is a valid, optional extra.
Restricting the port 22 ingress cidr_blocks to trusted ranges instead of 0.0.0.0/0 fixes CKV_AWS_24. It names the right block and attribute, though it gives no example value.
